requirement:
Sections use `section`, named from whitespace-normalized heading text. ATX and
setext headings are supported. Content before the first heading can form an
anonymous section. Section nesting follows heading levels; other outline items
appear beneath their nearest enclosing container. Selectors follow
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
rationale:
structural: No implementation roots were supplied, and `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.sections` has no Implements edges. I found no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence.

The text is: "Sections use `section`, named from whitespace-normalized heading text. ATX and setext headings are supported. Content before the first heading can form an anonymous section. Section nesting follows heading levels; other outline items appear beneath their nearest enclosing container. Selectors follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`."

Each clause describes the outline the Markdown source produces:
- **Item kind `section`:** this is the kind name in the selector, such as `section[Title]`. It is an observable output. A different parser, such as a hand-written scanner instead of a Markdown library, would give the same selectors and would still satisfy it.
- **Whitespace-normalized names:** this is an output rule. Any normalization routine meets it.
- **ATX and setext headings:** this is a supported-input behavior. The text names no parser library or algorithm.
- **Anonymous leading section:** the clause says "can" (permissive), and it describes output.
- **Nesting by heading level, and other items under their nearest container:** this is the shape of the output tree, not a prescribed type or delegation.
- **Selectors follow `requirements.references.outline_selectors`:** this is a cited requirement. It supplies context and is not a structural obligation of this requirement.

The text prescribes no library, signature, type, field or named interface. Tests supply the evidence for these behaviors.

behavioral: The supplied tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.sections`, and their assertions enforce the expected outcomes.

- **`section` kind and whitespace-normalized names.**
  - `markdown_profile_nests_sections_by_heading` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs` checks that `# Head  *one*` becomes `section[Head%20*one*]`.
  - `markdown_sections_include_setext_headings_and_anonymous_preamble` checks that `Heading   words` becomes `section[Heading%20words]`.
  - `multiline_setext_sections_keep_original_source_spans_and_skip_code` checks that a two-line setext heading `Títle\ntwo` becomes `section[Títle%20two]`.
- **ATX and setext headings.**
  - ATX headings are covered in several tests.
  - Setext headings are covered at level 1 (`===`) in `markdown_sections_include_setext_headings_and_anonymous_preamble`.
  - Level 2 (`---`) is covered in `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items`.
  - Multi-line setext headings, and `===` inside a code fence not being treated as a heading, are covered in `multiline_setext_sections_keep_original_source_spans_and_skip_code`.
  - Setext headings inside directives, quotes and lists are covered in `setext_sections_inside_directives_lists_and_quotes_retain_container_spans`.
- **Anonymous preamble section.**
  - `markdown_sections_include_setext_headings_and_anonymous_preamble` checks that the first section selector starts with `section@`.
  - `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` checks the same and checks the text `préface`.
  - `markdown_profile_nests_sections_by_heading` checks the preamble with front matter present.
- **Nesting follows heading levels.**
  - Sub-sections nest under their parent in the tests above.
  - A skipped level (`#` then `###`) nests `Deep` under `Main`.
  - Duplicate `Same` sections get `#1` and `#2`.
  - A setext level-2 `Level two` nests under `End`, and a later `## Peer` is a sibling of `Level two` under `End`.
  - A new `# End` closes the previous sections.
  - Section spans are checked, for example `second` does not contain `first`, and `# Last` is not in the `Parent` sub-section.
- **Other items under the nearest enclosing container.**
  - `paragraphs_and_nested_directives_have_independent_source_ranges` checks the parent indexes for paragraphs, blocks, and a paragraph inside a nested block.
  - `markdown_profile_nests_sections_by_heading` checks paragraphs under sections.
  - `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` checks that a block is under `section[End]/section[Level%20two]`.
- **Selectors follow `requirements.references.outline_selectors`.**
  - This is a cited requirement, so only its application here needs checking.
  - The tests assert percent-encoded special characters (`/`, `[`, `]`, `#`, `@`, `%`) in names.
  - They assert `#n` duplicate disambiguation and `@` anonymous segments.
  - They check that selectors round-trip through `resolve` and `select`.

I found no requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept.
